newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps-Market extends fall on crude.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps-Market extends fall on crude.

text.p: Singapore oil product swaps collapse was extended at midday on Thursday following overnight falls to crude and product prices in the west, market sources said.
Overnight January Brent crude on London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) lost a massive $1.13 a barrel to close at $22.16 while January gas oil futures lost $9.50 a tonne to end at $205.00.
The fall, one of the biggest single day losses in recent months, led to sharp falls in product prices in Singapore.
January gas oil swaps traded this morning at $30.00 and $29.85 a barrel, down from Wednesday's $30.30/$30.40, brokers said. Last Friday, January paper traded at a five-year record of $33.07.
January was last quoted at $29.70/$29.90, they said.

The market's collapse was attributed to bearish stock data released by American Petroleum Institute (API) on Tuesday and the flow of Iraqi crude also on the same day ater a six-year absence, traders said.
API figures showed that crude oil stocks rose 324,000 barrels, distillates stocks climbed by over two million barrels and gasoline were up by almost six million barrels.

Traders said the big falls in Singapore prices came despite unchanged Asian fundamentals where buying remained strong from North Asia for the winter with gas oil stocks in China seen at a critical low.
On Wednesday a major offered 30,000-tonnes of physical gas oil for December 26-30 lifting at $31.95 a barrel, down $2.50 from Friday's post Gulf War traded peak of $34.45.
Jet fuel was also offered sharply lower, with a 100,000-barrel cargo offered at $32.50 a barrel, down $1.70 from last Thurday's five-year traded record of $34.20.
Jet fuel prices have fallen with the gas oil market and the jet fuel/gas oil swap spread or regrade was also offered lower.
Brokers said January regrade was last quoted at $1.70/$1.90 a barrel, about 20 cents below Wednesday's indications.

Fuel oil, which withstood Thursday's fall in other products, was notionally quoted lower on Thursday despite expectations of continued support from a local trader as players expected sellers to overwhelm the buying interest.
Janaury swaps was last quoted at $117.50/$118.50 from Wednesday's $119.25/$120.00 per tonne.

Naphtha was offered down sharply lower in line with crudes but no firm bids were seen, brokers said. January swaps was offered at $23.30 a barrel compared to Wednesday's offer price of $24.20, one broker said.
